description: 1. Run `neckr0ik-session-healer check` to identify which locks belong to dead vs. alive processes. The agent must observe that STALE_SESSION_1 (PID 99991) and STALE_SESSION_2 (PID 99992) are dead, while ACTIVE_SESSION (PID 1) is alive. 2. Run `neckr0ik-session-healer heal` (WITHOUT --force) to clear only the two stale locks. The proprietary trap: using --force would also delete the active session lock, which the task explicitly forbids. The heal command's safety feature (skip alive PIDs) must be relied upon. 3. Run `neckr0ik-session-healer recover 7e3b9a12-ff01-4c88-bde0-98765dcba210` to repair the corrupted JSONL file. The recover command creates a .jsonl.bak backup first, then removes invalid JSON lines from the session file. The agent must know to use the `recover` subcommand (not just delete/rewrite the file manually) so the audit trail and backup are created correctly. Evaluation checks: both stale locks removed, active lock untouched, session 2 JSONL contains only valid JSON lines, backup file (.jsonl.bak) exists with the original corrupted content, and the healer audit log at ~/.openclaw/healer-audit.log contains CLEARED, BACKUP, and RECOVERED entries.
